# fptcloud_backup_native_vm_restore_points_purge (Resource)

Deletes every Backup Native restore point of a VM. It deletes the restore points taken under every job, past and current, and frees their backup quota; the VM's next backup is a full backup. Applying the resource waits while a backup or restore of the VM runs, starts the deletion and waits for it to end. Destroying the resource only removes it from state; deleted restore points cannot be recovered. Change a value in `triggers` to delete the restore points again. Run one purge per VM at a time; two concurrent purges of the same VM can be matched to the wrong history row.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Deletes every restore point of the VM, under any backup job, and waits for
# the deletion to end. The VM's next backup is a full backup.
# Set purge to the time you ask for the deletion; a new time deletes the
# restore points again, and the state records when each purge was requested.
# Write the time as a literal: timestamp() changes on every plan and deletes
# the restore points on every apply.
resource "fptcloud_backup_native_vm_restore_points_purge" "web" {
  vpc_id   = var.vpc_id
  vm_id    = var.web_instance_id
  triggers = { purge = "2026-10-26 09:00:00" }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `vm_id` (String) ID of the VM whose restore points are deleted. The VM does not need to be in a backup job.
- `vpc_id` (String) ID of the VPC.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Values that delete the restore points again when they change, which no other argument can express because every other argument stays equal. Set each value to the time you ask for the action, in the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, for example `2026-10-26 09:00:00`, so the state records when each one was requested. Write the time as a literal: `timestamp()` changes on every plan and repeats the action on every apply.

### Read-Only

- `finished_at` (String) When the provider saw the purge end, RFC 3339 UTC.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `restore_point_count` (Number) Number of restore points the VM had when the purge started. `0` means there was nothing to delete and no request was sent.
- `started_at` (String) When the provider started the purge, RFC 3339 UTC.
- `status` (String) Result of the purge, `Success` after a successful apply.
